method: Read-only retrieval of public repository source via the GitLab files API, then direct inspection of the exact files and lines named in an operator-supplied technical writeup. No repository was cloned, modified or executed. Nothing here is an exploitation procedure.

claims_verified.bug: batched MsgDeposit overwrites one voter keyed on the shared tx id
claims_verified.observed: NewObservedTxVoter(txIn.Tx.ID, []ObservedTx{txIn}) then SetObservedTxInVoter(ctx, txInVoter), constructed fresh rather than fetched and appended

claims_verified.bug: outbound matcher walks heights by a fixed stride and can skip the true height
claims_verified.observed: outHeight := voter.OutboundHeight; if zero, falls back to voter.FinalisedHeight; then for height := outHeight; height <= ctx.BlockHeight(); height += signingTransPeriod

claims_verified.bug: subsidy value computed from a pool ratio with no cap by the pool's asset balance
claims_verified.observed: runeValue := pool.AssetValueInRune(coin.Amount) inside subsidizePoolWithSlashBondV92; the only subsequent test is runeValue.IsZero(); no comparison against pool.BalanceAsset

claims_verified.bug: pool balance committed before the transfer meant to fund it
claims_verified.observed: pool.BalanceCacao = pool.BalanceCacao.Add(f.subsidiseRune) then SetPool(ctx, pool), and only afterwards SendFromModuleToModule(ctx, ReserveName, AsgardName, ...) whose failure returns an error with the pool write already persisted

claims_verified.bug: dispatcher logs the handler error and continues in the same context
claims_verified.observed: _, err = handler(ctx, m); on error: Logger().Error("handler failed:"), slashObservedOutbound("failed_outbound"), voter.SetDone(), SetObservedTxOutVoter(...), continue — no cache context, no rollback

claims_verified.bug: pool unit dilution via near-zero-asset add liquidity

INC-2026-08-18-MAY.grade_effect: Five of six claimed defects were confirmed at the exact file and line stated, against live public source. Under the run's grading rule this is deployed-code evidence, so the record moves from B (SlowMist mechanism record only) to A.

upstream_check.question: Does THORChain, the $61.9M upstream of this fork, carry the same defects?
evidence: x/thorchain/helpers.go contains no subsidizePoolWithSlashBond* function; its AssetValueInRune call sites (937, 1078, 1286) are in unrelated functions, and SetPool(ctx, pool) appears once (line 317) outside a subsidy path.

x/thorchain/handler_common_outbound.go does not use the plain stride loop. It computes a per-chain searchPeriod (xmrSigningPeriodMultiplier, evmAggregatorSigningPeriodMultiplier, evmTokenSigningPeriodMultiplier, lines 98-105) and its comment states the window is bounded by 'one signingTransPeriod ago, whichever is later'.
x/thorchain/handler_deposit.go constructs its voter at lines 215-219 with different surrounding structure.
x/thorchain/handler_observed_txout.go is 2,855 bytes against Maya's 12,418; the dispatcher shape differs.
upstream_check.disposition: The obvious lineage lead is KILLED on evidence. The two codebases have diverged materially; the defects verified on Maya are Maya's, not inherited shape still present upstream. Recorded so the negative result is auditable rather than silently dropped.
upstream_check.caveat: This compares the current develop branch of each repository. It establishes that these five shapes are not present there now. It is not a general safety statement about THORChain, and no other defect class was searched for.
